text:
incident-bot: 🚨 LATENCY SLO BREACH detected on shared-gpu-pool-us-east - p99 > 10s, p95 ~ 4.5s. Auto-pager fired.

sara: seeing the alert, jumping in. p95/p99 graph: p95 jumped from 120ms -> 4.5s around 02:02 UTC. p99 peaked ~12s.

mike: confirming, also seeing streaming stalls. KStreams shows stalled chunks at 3-8s intervals, clients time out and retry.

lee: oncall handoff incoming in 10m — @mike you'll be primary after that. Sara, any signs of increased GPU utilization or IO?

sara: GPU util % is normal on most nodes, but one host nvme_io_wait is high (iostat shows ~60% util). blkio latency spikes on cgroup  `tenant-42`.

anya: FYI customer Slack: ParkwayDocs is reporting intermittent streaming stalls and degraded generation for two customers. They called severity P1.

mike: running quick tenant query: `rgw-top --pool shared-gpu-pool-us-east --top-cgroups` shows tenant-42 at top for bytes_written and disk-reads. Suspect noisy neighbor hitting NVMe IO causing tail latency.

lee: can we confirm cgroup limits? show `cat /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-42/blkio.throttle.*` or `blkio.weight`?

sara: grabbing values now.

sara: output: `blkio.weight=500` (default 500), `blkio.throttle.read_bps_device` empty, but `io.stat` shows read latency high. Also `nvidia-smi dmon` doesn't show abnormal GPU mem use, so it's IO-bound.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily evict or throttle tenant-42 IO, 2) drain critical customers off shared pool to dedicated nodes, 3) enable prefix KV caching to reduce reads.

tim: if we evict tenant-42 unattended we'll cause their jobs to fail. recommend throttling via blkio throttle first. Command to set read bps: 
```
# throttle reads to 100MB/s on device major:minor (example)
echo "259:0 104857600" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/tenant-42/blkio.throttle.read_bps_device
```

mike: doing throttle now on host gpu-host-7.

mike: throttle applied. Observability: p95 dropped from 4.5s -> 900ms in ~90s. p99 now ~3.2s. streaming stalls reduced but still present.

anya: customer impact update: ParkwayDocs critical routes seeing 40% requests >2s before throttle, now ~12%. Cliply reported 5% errors earlier, now 1%. I'll message affected customers with ETA for full remediation.

lee: good progress. Next: move high-priority routes off shared pool. @deploy-bot can you start early-route reassignments for ParkwayDocs and AcmeAI?

deploy-bot: queued route reassignments: ParkwayDocs -> dedicated-gpu-03, AcmeAI -> dedicated-gpu-02. Estimated cutover 4m.

mike: traffic rerouted. Confirming connections: dedicated nodes have lower IO contention. p99 trending down to ~1.1s after reroute.

sara: follow-up: we should identify why tenant-42 is IO-heavy. Could be a large batch offline job hitting local NVMe. Requesting tenant-42 owner contact.

mike: digging into traces — heavy sequential reads on /dev/nvme0n1 initiated by a job labeled `bulk-indexer-v2` started at 01:58 UTC. That job was queued by internal ML training pipeline for embeddings.

lee: action items now: 1) escalate with tenant-42 owner to throttle their pipeline and move it to dedicated batch nodes; 2) add automatic blkio throttle rule to prevent single tenant from using >40% of device bandwidth; 3) create a post-incident follow-up to evaluate pool sizing and guardrails.

anya: I've sent interim customer notices for ParkwayDocs and Cliply. They want a postmortem and timeline.

mike: creating mitigation PR with temporary `blkio-throttle-by-tenant` rule and adding metric alert for NVME io_wait > 40% sustained for 2m.

sara: also adding a streaming-specific SLO check: detect >5% stream stalls in a 5m window and auto-failover to dedicated models for enterprise customers.

lee: oncall handoff — @mike you'll take incident lead for the next hour, then @tim will be secondary. Escalate to platform oncall if p99 > 5s again.

mike: noted. I'll keep this thread updated with timeline and remediation tickets.

anya: customer impact summary to include in postmortem: ParkwayDocs (prod) — sustained tail latency spike causing degraded streaming; Cliply — transient errors during peak; internal bulk-indexer (tenant-42) responsible for noisy IO.

sara: final note for now: after throttle + reroute p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~1.1s, streaming stalls near zero. Closing pager for shared-gpu-pool-us-east. Will file a follow-up with incident timeline and RCA steps.

mike: thanks all. Will create the incident ticket and link the follow-up RFC for stronger multi-tenant IO guardrails.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE recorded: severity lowered to SEV3 at 02:28 UTC.
